_comment: How this language's phrases hold together, for lib/chunker.py. Optional, like every file of this name.
_why: Arabic puts the adjective after its noun (الكتاب الكبير) and its prepositions before the noun (في البيت); the idafa binds forward the way the Persian ezafe does.
_question_words: The words that open a question, for tidy.py alone: an automatic transcript that carries no punctuation gets a question mark where a sentence opens (or, in a verb-final language, ends) with one of these, and a full stop otherwise. A language whose transcript IS punctuated needs none of this -- the mark is already in the text -- so only the languages YouTube leaves bare list them.
_question_any: ...and of those, the ones that can ONLY ask: a question particle, which means a question wherever in the sentence it stands. The rest are read at the edges alone, because they mean other things in the middle of one.
